one_line: A learned Pallava-Grantha scribe from Kanchipuram whose work helps carry Sanskrit prestige and administrative writing across South and Southeast Asia.

appearance.face: oval face, warm medium-brown South Indian complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, sharp attentive eyes with a calm scholarly gaze, default expression focused yet gentle as if mid-thought
appearance.hair: thick black hair oiled and combed back into a modest low bun at the back of the head, front kept smooth without loose strands, adorned with a simple narrow white cotton headband tied around the forehead
appearance.costume: era-accurate South Indian Brahmin-scribe attire: a full-length off-white cotton dhoti wrapped securely from waist to ankles in the Tamil style with a neat front pleat, paired with a light cream-colored long-sleeved cotton angavastra-style upper cloth worn like a fitted tunic covering the torso and arms, a second pale yellow angavastra draped over the left shoulder and across the chest, thin red woven border along the dhoti and shoulder cloth edges, a simple sacred thread diagonally under the tunic but subtly indicated, bare feet in plain brown leather sandals; minimal jewellery limited to a small gold stud in each ear and a single black-thread wrist amulet on the right hand
appearance.signature: a dark brown palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a thin cord in the left hand and a slender metal stylus held delicately in the right hand, tip slightly darkened to suggest frequent use

ref_desc: A mid-30s South Indian scribe with an oval medium-brown face, short beard, black hair in a low bun with white headband, wearing off-white dhoti, cream tunic, pale yellow angavastra with red borders, brown sandals, holding a palm-leaf manuscript and metal stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of a mid-30s South Indian Pallava-Grantha scribe: he has an oval medium-brown face, sharp yet gentle eyes, straight nose, and a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache; his thick black hair is combed back into a low bun at the back of the head, with a simple narrow white cotton headband tied around his forehead. He wears era-accurate South Indian Brahmin-scribe clothing: a full-length off-white cotton dhoti wrapped from waist to ankles in neat Tamil-style folds with a thin red woven border, a light cream long-sleeved upper garment fitted to the torso, and a second pale yellow angavastra draped over his left shoulder and across his chest, also edged with a fine red border. A subtle sacred thread line is hinted beneath the tunic, and his feet are in plain brown leather sandals. Jewellery is minimal—a small gold stud in each ear and a single black-thread wrist amulet on his right hand. In his left hand he carries a tightly bundled dark brown palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord, and in his right hand he holds a slender metal stylus with a slightly darkened tip, posed in a way that suggests poised, careful writing. Use off-white, cream, pale yellow, red accents, and dark brown as the dominant colours, and show front, side, and back views to capture his face, hair, garments, and scholarly tools clearly.
